jp: 母[はは]は子[こ]どもに野菜[やさい]を{食[た]べさせました|pt-causative}。
en: Mother made her child eat vegetables.
d: 食[た]べさせられました
why: Mother makes the child eat, so the causative -させる is needed.

jp: 先生[せんせい]は生徒[せいと]に毎日[まいにち]日記[にっき]を{書[か]かせています|pt-causative}。
en: The teacher has his students write a diary every day.
why: The teacher makes the students write: causative -せる, not the passive.

jp: 部長[ぶちょう]は新入社員[しんにゅうしゃいん]に会議[かいぎ]の資料[しりょう]を{作[つく]らせた|pt-causative}。
en: The manager made the new employee prepare the meeting documents.
why: The manager gives the order, so the causative 作らせる fits.

jp: 父[ちち]は弟[おとうと]に自分[じぶん]の進路[しんろ]を{選[えら]ばせた|pt-causative}。
en: Father let my younger brother choose his own path.
why: Father allows the brother to choose: causative of 選ぶ, brother as chooser.

jp: あの映画[えいが]は観客[かんきゃく]を{泣[な]かせました|pt-causative}。
en: That film made the audience cry.
why: The film causes the audience's crying; an intransitive verb takes causative with を.

jp: 姉[あね]は冗談[じょうだん]を言[い]って、みんなを{笑[わら]わせた|pt-causative}。
en: My sister told a joke and made everybody laugh.
why: The sister makes others laugh, so the causative 笑わせる is used.

jp: 医者[いしゃ]は患者[かんじゃ]さんにしばらく運動[うんどう]を{やめさせました|pt-causative}。
en: The doctor made the patient stop exercising for a while.
why: The doctor orders the patient to stop: causative やめさせる.

jp: 母[はは]は妹[いもうと]を一人[ひとり]で買[か]い物[もの]に{行[い]かせました|pt-causative}。
en: Mother sent my little sister shopping by herself.
why: Mother sends the sister off: causative 行かせる, sister marked by を.

jp: 遅[おそ]くなってごめん。心配[しんぱい]{させて|pt-causative}しまったね。
en: Sorry I'm late. I made you worry, didn't I?
why: The speaker caused the other person's worry, so the causative させる is needed.

jp: 監督[かんとく]は選手[せんしゅ]たちを毎朝[まいあさ]グラウンドで{走[はし]らせます|pt-causative}。
en: The coach makes the players run on the field every morning.
why: The coach orders the running: causative of 走る.

jp: 父[ちち]は息子[むすこ]に庭[にわ]の草[くさ]を{抜[ぬ]かせました|pt-causative}。
en: Father made his son pull the weeds in the garden.
why: Father gives the order and the son works, so the causative 抜かせる is needed.

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]は社員[しゃいん]に毎年[まいとし]健康診断[けんこうしんだん]を{受[う]けさせます|pt-causative}。
en: The company has its employees take a health check every year.
why: The company makes employees take the check-up: causative 受けさせる.

jp: 母[はは]は、子[こ]どもに宿題[しゅくだい]を早[はや]く{させたい|pt-causative}と思[おも]っている。
en: Mother wants to make her child do his homework early.
why: Mother wants the child to do it, so causative させる + たい is needed.

jp: 先生[せんせい]は学生[がくせい]に来週[らいしゅう]までにレポートを{書[か]かせる|pt-causative}つもりです。
en: The teacher intends to make the students write a report by next week.
why: The teacher decides what the students will do: causative 書かせる + つもり.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]は孫[まご]を庭[にわ]で{遊[あそ]ばせて|pt-causative}います。
en: Grandmother is letting her grandchild play in the garden.
why: Grandmother lets the child play: causative of 遊ぶ.

jp: 店長[てんちょう]はアルバイトに閉店後[へいてんご]の掃除[そうじ]を{させています|pt-causative}。
en: The shop manager has the part-timers clean up after closing.
why: The manager assigns the cleaning to others: causative させる.

jp: 先生[せんせい]は生徒[せいと]に重[おも]い荷物[にもつ]を{持[も]たせました|pt-causative}。
en: The teacher made the students carry the heavy luggage.
why: The teacher orders the carrying, so 持たせる is the causative.

jp: 母[はは]は赤[あか]ちゃんに薬[くすり]を{飲[の]ませました|pt-causative}。
en: Mother gave the baby its medicine (made the baby take it).
why: Mother makes the baby take the medicine: causative 飲ませる.

jp: 彼[かれ]の言葉[ことば]は母[はは]を{怒[おこ]らせて|pt-causative}しまった。
en: His words made my mother angry.
why: His words cause the mother's anger: causative 怒らせる, not 怒られる (be scolded).

jp: 約束[やくそく]の時間[じかん]に遅[おく]れて、友達[ともだち]を三十分[さんじゅっぷん]も{待[ま]たせてしまった|pt-causative}。
en: I was late and kept my friend waiting for thirty minutes.
d: 待[ま]たされてしまった
why: The speaker made the friend wait: causative 待たせる, not the causative-passive.

jp: 学生[がくせい]に自分[じぶん]で答[こた]えを{考[かんが]えさせる|pt-causative}のが、あの先生[せんせい]のやり方[かた]だ。
en: That teacher's method is to make the students think up the answer themselves.
d: 考[かんが]えさせられる
why: The teacher makes the students think: plain causative 考えさせる.

jp: 夫[おっと]は子[こ]どもたちを{寝[ね]かせて|pt-causative}から、本[ほん]を読[よ]み始[はじ]めた。
en: After putting the children to bed, my husband started to read a book.
why: The husband makes the children sleep: causative 寝かせる.

jp: 社長[しゃちょう]は若[わか]い社員[しゃいん]に海外[かいがい]で経験[けいけん]を{積[つ]ませた|pt-causative}。
en: The president had the young employee gain experience abroad.
why: The president sends the employee to gain experience: causative 積ませる.

jp: 母[はは]は娘[むすめ]にピアノを{習[なら]わせて|pt-causative}いる。
en: Mother has her daughter take piano lessons.
why: The mother arranges it and the daughter learns: causative 習わせる.

jp: 彼[かれ]はいつも私[わたし]を{困[こま]らせる|pt-causative}。
en: He always causes me trouble.
why: He is the cause and I am troubled: causative 困らせる.

jp: 子[こ]どもには好[す]きな本[ほん]を自由[じゆう]に{読[よ]ませる|pt-causative}のが、うちの方針[ほうしん]です。
en: Our policy is to let children read whatever books they like.
why: We allow the children to read: permissive causative 読ませる.

jp: 私[わたし]は子[こ]どものころ、母[はは]に嫌[きら]いな野菜[やさい]を{食[た]べさせられました|pt-causative}。
en: As a child I was made by my mother to eat vegetables I hated.
why: I am the one forced, so the causative-passive 食べさせられる is needed.

jp: 昨日[きのう]は部長[ぶちょう]に夜[よる]十時[じゅうじ]まで残業[ざんぎょう]{させられました|pt-causative}。
en: Yesterday the manager made me work overtime until ten p.m.
why: I was forced to work overtime: causative-passive させられる.

jp: 先生[せんせい]に漢字[かんじ]を百回[ひゃっかい]{書[か]かされました/書[か]かせられました|pt-causative}。
en: I was made by the teacher to write the kanji a hundred times.
why: I was forced to write: causative-passive 書かされる (書かせられる).

jp: 新人[しんじん]のころ、先輩[せんぱい]に毎晩[まいばん]お酒[さけ]を{飲[の]まされた/飲[の]ませられた|pt-causative}。
en: When I was new, my seniors made me drink every night.
why: The speaker was forced to drink: causative-passive 飲まされる.

jp: 弟[おとうと]は兄[あに]に重[おも]い荷物[にもつ]を{持[も]たされて/持[も]たせられて|pt-causative}、文句[もんく]を言[い]っていた。
en: My younger brother was made to carry heavy bags by our older brother and was complaining.
why: The younger brother was forced: causative-passive 持たされる.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]で急[きゅう]に意見[いけん]を求[もと]められて、みんなの前[まえ]で{話[はな]させられた|pt-causative}。
en: I was suddenly asked for my opinion at the meeting and made to speak in front of everyone.
why: I was forced to speak: causative-passive 話させられる (only the long form for 話す).

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]に三時間[さんじかん]も{待[ま]たされた/待[ま]たせられた|pt-causative}。
en: My girlfriend made me wait for three hours.
why: I was kept waiting against my wish: causative-passive 待たされる.

jp: あの映画[えいが]を見[み]て、人生[じんせい]について{考[かんが]えさせられた|pt-causative}。
en: That film made me think about life.
why: The film caused my reflection: causative-passive 考えさせられる.

jp: 上司[じょうし]に無理[むり]な仕事[しごと]を{やらされて/やらせられて|pt-causative}、毎日[まいにち]疲[つか]れている。
en: My boss makes me do impossible jobs, and I am tired every day.
why: The boss forces the work on me: causative-passive やらされる.

jp: 友達[ともだち]の引[ひ]っ越[こ]しで、一日[いちにち]中[じゅう]荷物[にもつ]を{運[はこ]ばされた/運[はこ]ばせられた|pt-causative}。
en: At my friend's move I was made to carry boxes all day.
why: I was put to work against my wish: causative-passive 運ばされる.

jp: 子[こ]どものころ、父[ちち]に毎朝[まいあさ]ふとんを{畳[たた]まされた/畳[たた]ませられた|pt-causative}。
en: When I was a child, my father made me fold up the futon every morning.
why: I was the one made to fold it: causative-passive 畳まされる.

jp: 授業[じゅぎょう]中[ちゅう]に騒[さわ]いで、先生[せんせい]に廊下[ろうか]に{立[た]たされた/立[た]たせられた|pt-causative}。
en: I made noise in class and was made to stand in the corridor by the teacher.
why: I was forced to stand as punishment: causative-passive 立たされる.

jp: 夏休[なつやす]みの間[あいだ]、おじの店[みせ]でずっと皿[さら]を{洗[あら]わされた/洗[あら]わせられた|pt-causative}。
en: During the summer vacation I was made to wash dishes at my uncle's shop the whole time.
why: I was put to work by my uncle: causative-passive 洗わされる.

jp: 新入社員[しんにゅうしゃいん]は歓迎会[かんげいかい]で歌[うた]を{歌[うた]わされた/歌[うた]わせられた|pt-causative}。
en: The new employees were made to sing at the welcome party.
why: The new employees were forced to sing: causative-passive 歌わされる.

jp: 彼[かれ]の話[はなし]に、思[おも]わず{笑[わら]わされた/笑[わら]わせられた|pt-causative}。
en: His story made me laugh in spite of myself.
why: His story caused my laughter: causative-passive 笑わされる.

jp: 社長[しゃちょう]の自慢話[じまんばなし]を、二時間[にじかん]も{聞[き]かされた/聞[き]かせられた|pt-causative}。
en: I was made to listen to the president's boasting for two hours.
why: I had to listen against my wish: causative-passive 聞かされる.

jp: 試験[しけん]の前[まえ]に、先生[せんせい]に問題[もんだい]を何度[なんど]も{解[と]かされた/解[と]かせられた|pt-causative}。
en: Before the exam the teacher made me solve the problems over and over.
why: The teacher forced me to solve them: causative-passive 解かされる.

jp: 雨[あめ]の中[なか]、彼[かれ]は妹[いもうと]の買[か]い物[もの]に{付[つ]き合[あ]わされた/付[つ]き合[あ]わせられた|pt-causative}。
en: In the rain, he was made to go along on his sister's shopping.
why: He was dragged along: causative-passive 付き合わされる.

jp: 取引先[とりひきさき]の前[まえ]で、部長[ぶちょう]に{謝[あやま]らされた/謝[あやま]らせられた|pt-causative}。
en: In front of the client, the manager made me apologize.
why: I was forced to apologize: causative-passive 謝らされる (or 謝らせられる).

jp: 姉[あね]は母[はは]に弟[おとうと]の面倒[めんどう]を{見[み]させられた|pt-causative}。
en: My older sister was made by Mother to look after our younger brother.
why: The sister was ordered to do it: causative-passive 見させられる.

jp: あの先生[せんせい]の授業[じゅぎょう]では、学生[がくせい]は毎回[まいかい]前[まえ]に出[で]て発表[はっぴょう]{させられる|pt-causative}。
en: In that teacher's class the students are made to go up front and give a presentation every time.
why: Students are forced to present: causative-passive させられる.

jp: 兄[あに]は母[はは]に庭[にわ]の草[くさ]を{抜[ぬ]かされた/抜[ぬ]かせられた|pt-causative}。
en: My older brother was made by Mother to pull the weeds in the garden.
why: The brother was ordered to work: causative-passive 抜かされる.

jp: 辞[や]めたくなかったのに、会社[かいしゃ]を{辞[や]めさせられた|pt-causative}。
en: Although I did not want to quit, I was forced to leave the company.
why: Quitting was forced on me: causative-passive 辞めさせられる.

jp: 試合[しあい]に負[ま]けた罰[ばつ]で、グラウンドを十周[じっしゅう]{走[はし]らされた/走[はし]らせられた|pt-causative}。
en: As punishment for losing the match, we were made to run ten laps of the field.
why: We were forced to run as punishment: causative-passive 走らされる.
